trial_court: Principal Judge, Family Court, at Bangalore (M.C.No.1106/2012)
case_name: Sri K N Anil vs Smt Deepika Nair
facts_of_case: Petitioner's marriage with respondent was solemnised according to Hindu rites on 07-05-2008. Respondent's mother interfered in their marital life by giving instructions over telephone, creating problems. Petitioner sought divorce under Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party alleging cruelty to prove it beyond doubt.
legal_principles.held: Whether the petitioner (husband) has proved beyond doubt that, there was alleged cruelty by the respondent (wife), attracting Section 13 (1)(ia) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955?

legal_principles.principle: A party's readiness and willingness to join the other in the matrimonial home is a relevant factor in determining desertion.
legal_principles.held: However, she has been ready and willing to join her husband in her matrimonial home, however, the petitioner (husband) and his parents are not ready to take her back

outcome.final_order: The judgment dated 21-02-2015 passed by the Principal Judge, Family Court, at Bangalore was set aside and the appeal was allowed.

keywords: Latin maxim: Nemo dat quod non habet
use_for_drafting: preparing judgment on maintenance and custody
advising client on residency requirements for divorce
